## Overview

Adyen's 2026-09-15 BACS Direct Debit Web Drop-in guide adds method-specific request and tokenization instructions to an existing Web Drop-in integration. It covers both Sessions and Advanced server-side flows. The page is integration guidance; a `Received` response is not final clearing or proof of funds. See [[adyen]] and [[adyen-online-payments]].

## Key takeaways

- Sessions requires an existing Web Drop-in Sessions integration, Checkout API v68 or later, and BACS added in Customer Area. The method-specific `/sessions` field is required `shopperEmail`. `BacsDirectDebit` is an optional individual import for tree shaking. The TEST/GBP/GB session examples use an app-style `adyencheckout://` return URL despite this Web page; treat it as a sample value, not a general Web return-URL rule. The main Sessions curl omits a shell continuation after `-X POST`, leaving `-d` outside the command as printed, so use it as a request illustration rather than copy-ready shell (raw lines 25-68, 341-351).
- Advanced requires an existing Web Drop-in Advanced integration, BACS added in Customer Area and additional-action handling. Its `/payments` table requires `shopperEmail`, `paymentMethod.type: directdebit_GB`, account holder name, bank account number and `bankLocationId` (the bank routing/sort-code value in the sample); the optional `BacsDirectDebit` import applies here too. The Advanced prerequisite link contains an encoded unresolved `getParameter('platform')` placeholder; nearby action and payment-step links explicitly use `platform=Web`, so the placeholder is not a verified base-guide route. The main Advanced curl also lacks a continuation after `-X POST`, leaving `-d` outside the command; it illustrates fields rather than copy-ready shell (raw lines 422-487). The prerequisite calls the action `Direct`, but the response section says `Direct` while the shown `Received` response contains `action.type: voucher` and `PDF_MANDATE_URL`. This source does not reconcile that discrepancy; handle the actual returned action under the base integration guidance rather than assuming the example is a guaranteed shape (raw lines 428-431, 819-832).
- For recurring, Adyen recommends tokenizing details and strongly recommends explicit shopper permission and transparent schedule/amount to reduce chargeback risk. This guide additionally states that a changed collection date or amount requires advance notice under the Direct Debit Guarantee, and strongly recommends notice before each payment. The initial token instructions specifically say to make a `/payments` request with `shopperReference` and `storePaymentMethod: true`; `recurring.token.created` supplies the `storedPaymentMethodId`. Later `/payments` examples use that ID, the same shopper reference and `shopperInteraction: ContAuth` (raw lines 353-406, 834-887).
- For recurring requests, the page says `paymentMethod.recurringDetailReference` or `paymentMethod.storedPaymentMethodId` for API v49 and above; this historical wording should not erase the explicit `storedPaymentMethodId` returned by its token webhook and used in its JSON example (raw lines 374-403, 855-884).
- The page says `Received` plus `pspReference` means a payment request was received and points to webhooks to track whether it succeeded. TEST bank details and test Customer Area status are provided; live BACS acceptance requires a separate request in live Customer Area (raw lines 406-420, 887-901). The method's DDI, clearing and chargeback lifecycle belongs to [[source-adyen-docs-payment-methods-bacs]]; this page does not by itself prove funds have cleared.

quotes.text: Make sure that you use Checkout API v68 or later.

Under the [Direct Debit Guarantee](https://www.directdebit.co.uk/direct-debit-explained/direct-debit-guarantee), if there is a change in the collection date or the amount, you must give the shopper advance notice of the payment.
When you receive the [recurring.token.created](https://docs.adyen.com/api-explorer/Tokenization-webhooks/latest/post/recurring.token.created), store the `storedPaymentMethodId`.
You can track whether the payment was successful using webhooks.
